content: How level-0 players behave and how they are perceived by higher-level players are central questions in the literature on level-k models of boundedly rational strategic reasoning. To investigate these issues, we use the intra-team communication method developed by Burchardi and Penczynski (2014) to identify level-0 actions and beliefs in both the canonical beauty contest game and a variant of the 11-20 game introduced by Goeree et al. (2018), where observed behavior appears inconsistent with the standard level-k model. In the beauty contest game, we replicate Burchardi and Penczynski’s (2014) finding that elicited level-0 beliefs closely align with observed level-0 actions. However, in the variant of the 11-20 game, elicited level-0 beliefs and observed level-0 actions diverge from each other and from the standard level-0 assumption. This divergence offers a complementary explanation for the behavioral patterns documented by Goeree et al. (2018).
